![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/dff61f08e09f21935f616788e54dfb56e0d0a89f38cce9fbc6dc7333d21ba5f1.png)

The scatter plot above gives the correspondence between the variables $x$ and $y$ for some data points.
Use the trend line to predict the value of $x$ when $y=80.$
question.worked_solution:
To make our prediction, we proceed as follows:

- First, we start at $y=80$ on the $y$-axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/e5923b6c9f0ac4dcf2aee35e67877c425b44f81830bb9f0865c5e21acf81e3f4.png)

- Then, we move right until we intersect the trend line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/613849314df8014335f7493f9b6b64cb4f2ecd1e585593416f416f1854e12ffa.png)

- Finally, we move down until we intersect the $x$-axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/4523e742266e3f2d2e759c6e65eb2a7f2bd31e8f4b8473b8e6bfbabec067c9d9.png)

Therefore, when $y=80,$ we obtain $x≈15.$
